column4: USDA FPL GTR-282 Chapter 5 pp. 5-42 to 5-43 Chemical Treatment and Waterborne Preservatives
column5: This is a historical 2021 handbook discussion of treatment effects, not current compliance authority. Effects depend on species, property, chemistry/type, retention, initial kiln drying, post-treatment drying, incising, size, grade, product type, temperature, and moisture. Retention at or below 16 kg/m3 (1.0 lb/ft3) is described as having no effect on MOE or compression strength parallel to grain, with slight negative tensile/bending effects; 40 kg/m3 (2.5 lb/ft3) is a higher reference level where MOR and energy-related properties are further reduced. Post-treatment redrying above 75 deg C is critical; 74 deg C (165 deg F) is the post-treatment kiln-redrying limitation cited in treatment standards. These are source process thresholds and qualitative effects, not universal correction factors. No species, preservative chemical, treatment schedule, grade, moisture, or retention-specific correction row is asserted; these remain data gaps.
